headline: Kai, everything waits on tomorrow's CPI — futures flat, the 10-year at 4.72 percent, and Brent pressing $88.
subline: Riot's $9.1 billion Anthropic deal, Zuckerberg's open-source manifesto, and a Hormuz agreement in final drafting share the front page.
asof: Pre-market · as of 6:40 AM ET · index figures are 4 AM futures · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Futures barely move on CPI eve
items.sentence: S&P 500 futures sit at 7,777.50, up 0.01 percent, Nasdaq futures add 0.07 percent and Dow futures slip 0.10 percent ahead of Wednesday's July inflation report, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: S&P 500 parks just under Friday's record
items.sentence: The cash index closed Monday at 7,750.12, down 0.06 percent and only a few points shy of Friday's record close, per Trading Economics.

items.title: The 10-year backs up to 4.72 percent
items.sentence: The yield sits at 4.72 percent, up about a basis point, per Trading Economics, as a soft July jobs report and Kevin Warsh's inflation-first Fed leave September hanging on tomorrow's number.

items.title: Brent presses $88 in Hormuz's sixth month
items.sentence: Brent adds 0.71 percent to $88.34 a barrel — up roughly a third over the past year, per Trading Economics — while reopening talks inch along.

items.title: Gold pauses after a 9 percent month
items.sentence: Spot gold eases 0.67 percent to $4,361.91 an ounce after gaining 9 percent over the past month, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Bitcoin steady near $64,000
items.sentence: Bitcoin stood at $63,949 late Monday, up 1.84 percent on the day, per CoinDesk, largely unmoved by the CPI countdown.

items.title: Iran and Oman near final Hormuz agreement
items.sentence: Tehran says the shipping-lane agreement with Muscat is in final drafting, with US conditions still open and a strait that carries a fifth of the world's oil and LNG shut since late February, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Ukraine hits another Russian oil facility
items.sentence: Kyiv's drone campaign against Russian fuel infrastructure is producing shortages and public unrest inside Russia, per NPR.

items.title: Assam flood deaths reach 100
items.sentence: Monsoon flooding in India's northeast has killed at least 100 people and pushed thousands from their homes, per NPR.

items.title: Washington pays developers to halt wind farms
items.sentence: The administration is paying companies billions in taxpayer funds to stop wind-farm projects already in development, per NPR.

items.title: Twenty million pilgrims converge on Iraq
items.sentence: Some 20 million Shia pilgrims gathered for Arbaeen at Iraq's shrine cities despite the region's conflicts, per NPR.

items.title: Zuckerberg bets Meta's AI future on open source
items.sentence: Alongside a manifesto arguing that concentrated control of AI by a few labs is the real danger, Meta released two open models — Muse Glimmer for personal computers and the stronger Muse Spark 1.2, per the AP.

items.title: Riot soars on $9.1 billion Anthropic deal
items.sentence: The bitcoin miner jumped 21 percent on reports of a $9.1 billion agreement to supply computing power to Anthropic, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Intel upsizes share sale toward $20 billion
items.sentence: Shares rose about 1 percent pre-market on reports the chipmaker will enlarge a planned share sale to roughly $20 billion, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: SpaceX touches its $135 IPO price again
items.sentence: The rocket maker traded back up to its $135 IPO price for the first time since mid-July, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Fermi lands $6.5 billion TensorWave lease
items.sentence: The datacenter developer surged 20 percent after signing its first binding customer lease, a $6.5 billion deal with TensorWave, per Yahoo Finance — AI demand is still writing very large checks.
